en.headline: Privacy watchdog arrests man for alleged doxxing over restaurant debt dispute
en.dek: A 37-year-old wholesale food supplier is suspected of disclosing personal details of a former restaurant operator and consultant online after a payment dispute, the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data said.
body: The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data arrested a 37-year-old wholesale food businessman on Tuesday on suspicion of doxxing two former associates following a financial dispute.

According to the PCPD, the suspect became acquainted with the male victim, then a restaurant operator, through a female business consultant in March 2025 and supplied frozen meat to the restaurant between March and May that year. A monetary dispute arose after a payment default and the parties could not reach agreement.

A year after the restaurant closed, a social-media post appeared accusing the male victim of defaulting on debts and urging internet users to track him down. The post disclosed the man’s English name, former schools, vehicle registration number, company name and address, family photos and a company registration screenshot.

The PCPD said the personal data of both victims was disclosed without consent. The arrested man was released on bail pending further investigation. The office reminded the public that doxxing over monetary disputes is illegal and can escalate conflicts.

zh.headline: 私隱專員公署拘男子涉因食肆欠款糾紛起底
zh.dek: 一名37歲凍肉批發商涉嫌在網上披露前餐廳東主及顧問的個人資料，私隱專員公署表示案件源於一宗付款爭議。
body: 個人資料私隱專員公署周二拘捕一名37歲凍肉批發商人，涉嫌因金錢糾紛起底兩名前合作人士。
公署指，涉案男子於2025年3月經一名女性商業顧問認識當時經營餐廳的男事主，其後於同年3月至5月向該餐廳供應急凍肉類。其後因拖欠款項出現金錢爭議，雙方未能達成協議。
餐廳結業約一年後，社交平台出現帖文指男事主拖欠債務，並呼籲網民追查其下落。帖文披露男事主英文姓名、前就讀學校、車牌號碼、公司名稱及地址、家庭照片，以及已結業公司的商業登記截圖。
公署表示，兩名事主的個人資料在未經同意下被披露。被捕男子已獲准保釋，案件仍在調查。公署提醒市民，因金錢糾紛起底屬違法行為，只會令衝突升級。
